newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU's Brittan sees two-thirds of EU members in EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan sees two-thirds of EU members in EMU.

text.p: European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Thursday he expected about two-thirds of European Union countries to make it into the first wave of entrants into European monetary union (EMU).
Brittan told a European forum in Paris he could see "two-thirds in the first wave" of monetary union.
Brittan also said he believed the effort to prepare for a single currency was good for the European and national economies because it obliged countries to address structural economic issues.
"In my opinion, the convergence criteria (in the Maastricht treaty) make European economies strong," he said.
"Take Italy and Spain...what we are seeing are decisions being taken on structural reform of the economy," he said, acknowledging that this drive had come "perhaps a little late in some cases."
